newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's El Nino dry weather seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Australia's El Nino dry weather seen continuing.

text.p: A strong El Nino weather event had produced a strong likelihood of significantly drier than normal conditions persisting and expanding across much of eastern and southern Australia, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Tuesday.

July rainfall across much of southern and eastern Australia was significantly below average, consistent with the continuing El Nino pattern, the bureau said in its latest monthly seasonal climate outlook.

Total rainfall since March also had reflected the developing El Nino episode with significantly below average rainfall for the period over South Australia, Victoria, parts of New South Wales (NSW) and Tasmania, it said.
The head of the bureau's national climate centre, Bill Kininmonth, said observational data continued to indicate a strong El Nino event at the end of July.
"The area of warm water in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean expanded and intensified," he said in the outlook.

Other signals retreated from recent extremes with the Pacific trade winds returning to near normal and the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) showing a rise of 14 points to minus 10, still a significantly low value, he said.
History showed that such short-term fluctuations were not unusual, he said.
More importantly, the persistence of very warm waters in the eastern and central Pacific was the the driving force behind the event, he said.
"Historical precedents and latest outputs from computer models point to a high probability of the El Nino continuing to evolve over coming months," he said.
"As a result there is a strong likelihood of significantly drier than normal conditions persisting and expanding across much of eastern and southern Australia," he said.

Areas most at risk of recording below average rainfall for the August to October period included most of Queensland, Victoria and Tasmania, southern and western NSW and eastern South Australia, he said.
El Nino is a weather pattern, caused by warm sea surface temperatures off South America, which produces drought in eastern Australia, Indonesia and nearby areas.
